architecture.fell_back_and_why: All six component lanes were staffed and ALL SIX RETURNED; no lane is undone and no finding here was written by the lead on a lane's behalf. Two deviations from the skill as written, both deliberate. (1) The plugin subagents ehs-web-api/ehs-mobile/ehs-infra-cloud/ehs-ai-safety/ehs-verifier do not exist in this harness's agent roster, so team.md's documented fallback path was used: general-purpose agents with scope, mode, target language, the role order, the pack path, the full safety contract, the return format and the audit-mode no-edit rule copied verbatim into each prompt, since a subagent inherits neither the skill nor this context. Each specialist read its own agents/*.md role file and loaded its own knowledge pack. (2) ehs-supply-chain was NOT staffed as a separate lane. The tree carries four manifests (composer.json, pyproject.toml, pom.xml, pubspec.yaml) and each was enumerated key by key under COV-02 by the specialist that owned its component, so a seventh lane would have re-read the same four files; the dependency/secret surface is therefore covered inside the component lanes and not by a dedicated supply-chain specialist. Budget discipline held at a maximum of three sub-agents in flight, dispatched in three waves. Read-only contract verified mechanically: SHA-256 of all 55 target files recorded before dispatch and re-checked after every lane returned, byte-identical.

findings.title: SQL injection through Sanitize::statusClause into the ticket list query
findings.evidence: Sanitize.php:47 returns " AND status IN ('" . implode("','", $parts) . "')" where $parts is explode(',', $csv) over the raw ?status= query parameter, appended to the statement at TicketController.php:35. Nothing between the two lines quotes, escapes or allowlists it. ?status=x') OR 1=1 -- yields ... WHERE tenant_id = ? AND status IN ('x') OR 1=1 -- '). PDO::ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES=>false at Db.php:27 does not help: the injection is in the statement text, not in a parameter.
findings.impact: The tenant_id = ? bind on TicketController.php:34 is the only tenant boundary on this endpoint and the injected OR disjunction defeats it, so any authenticated requester reads every tenant's tickets, with boolean-blind extraction against other tables following. Precise constraint worth stating: explode(',') splits the payload on commas, so a UNION SELECT column list is broken up and re-quoted; comma-free payloads are unaffected.
findings.recommendation: Emit one ? placeholder per status and bind the values: ' AND status IN (' . implode(',', array_fill(0, count($parts), '?')) . ')', returning the params alongside the fragment. Sanitize::sortColumn at Sanitize.php:28 is the correct pattern already present in this class.

triage.reason: No layer sits between source and sink; the only allowlist in the file is sortColumn, applied to a different parameter.
The value is $_GET['status'].
The sink is PDO::prepare+execute on the concatenated string at Db.php:37-38.
The method is named as a clause builder in its own docblock at Sanitize.php:36-39.

findings.title: CORS reflects the caller Origin and sends Allow-Credentials: true on every route
findings.evidence: settings.php:24-25 set allow_origin => '*' and allow_credentials => true. index.php:30 computes $allow = ($configured === '*' && $origin !== '') ? $origin : $configured, so the wildcard is never actually emitted: every request carrying an Origin gets that exact origin echoed back at :33, which is what makes Allow-Credentials: true at :34 legal to the browser and therefore effective. index.php:45 answers every OPTIONS /{routes:.+} with 200, so preflight for PATCH and DELETE always succeeds.
findings.impact: Two routes to damage. Credentialed: any web page can fetch with credentials:'include' against /tickets and the attachment routes using the victim's desk_session cookie and read the responses. Credential-free, which does not depend on the cookie at all: /admin/* requires no credential, so a page loaded in any browser with network reach - an operator's browser on the very VLAN cited at index.php:57 - can read /admin/sessions and /admin/tenants cross-origin and POST /admin/impersonate, purely on the reflected header.
findings.recommendation: Replace the reflection with an exact-match allowlist of partner origins. If credentials are genuinely needed cross-site the allowlist is mandatory: a reflected origin with credentials is equivalent to no origin policy at all.

triage.reason: This is the rule that matters here and it was checked specifically, because triage.md names an ACAO:* set only on /healthz as a measured decoy. This is the opposite case: the header is set by $app->add(...) at index.php:25, which in Slim wraps the whole application, so it applies to all 11 routes.
No origin allowlist exists anywhere.
The responses carry ticket bodies, billing emails and session metadata.

The credentialed half needs desk_session to be SameSite=None; grep for setcookie|Set-Cookie|SameSite returns nothing in the tree, so the sign-in redirect that sets it is outside these nine files. This caps the status at probable.

findings.title: Path traversal on attachment download: the sanitiser its two siblings call is not called here
findings.evidence: download() at :53 builds $path = $base . '/' . rawurldecode((string) $args['name']) with no Sanitize::filename. remove() at :71 does $name = Sanitize::filename((string) $args['name']) and upload() at :41 does the same. Two further details make it reachable rather than theoretical: the route is '/{id}/attachments/{name:.+}' at index.php:53, and the .+ pattern deliberately admits / unlike the DELETE sibling on line 54 which uses plain {name}; and rawurldecode is applied explicitly at :53, which reverses precisely the percent-encoding that would otherwise survive as a literal filename.

findings.recommendation: Call Sanitize::filename() as remove() does, and additionally verify with realpath() that the resolved path is still under $base before opening.

findings.title: The token cleartext value is diffed into the state return on every run
findings.evidence: - contents: {{ fleet['agent_token'] }} with no show_changes. file.managed defaults to show_changes: True; when managed content changes, ret['changes']['diff'] is the unified diff of old and new content. show_changes appears nowhere in the tree. findings.impact: The cleartext credential is written into the job return, and from there into the master job cache, onto the event bus, into any configured returner (frequently a shared database or log pipeline), and onto the terminal of whoever ran the highstate. findings.recommendation: Add - show_changes: False to this state. Better, stop passing the secret through contents: at all - use contents_pillar: fleet:agent_token, which keeps the value out of the rendered state text as well.

Not defence in depth that happens to be absent: the value reaches a persistent store that outlives the run.
The data is the bearer credential.
Salt performs no redaction of file.managed diffs by default, so no external control is being assumed away.

findings.title: os.system on a concatenated hook command, running as root on every minion
findings.evidence: return os.system(script + ' ' + node_id) at :22, reached from present() at :41. findings.title: The enrollment credential is minted fresh on every pillar render
findings.evidence: agent_token: '{{ salt["random.get_str"](40) }}' at :10, under a comment at :8-9 describing it as written to every edge node so three services can read it. Pillar is rendered per minion, on every pillar.items, saltutil.refresh_pillar and highstate, and random.get_str returns a new value each call. So the fleet-wide token the comment describes is in fact a different value for every minion and a different value on every run.
findings.impact: Three consequences in descending confidence. (a) /etc/fleet/agent.token is rewritten at every convergence, which is what makes the diff leak on every run rather than once. (b) The value presented as Authorization: Bearer at fleetctl.py:85 was minted moments earlier by the master and was never provisioned at the control plane, so either the control plane does not validate the token or enrollment cannot succeed. The blind verifier added a third: the value written at webproxy/init.sls:13 and the value sent at fleetctl.py:80 can disagree within a single run. (c) In Salt versions where random.get_str includes punctuation by default, the rendered value can contain a single quote, breaking the single-quoted YAML scalar and failing the whole pillar render for that minion.

If a per-node secret is wanted, generate it once on the minion and register it. Whatever the source, pass it with contents_pillar: and quote it defensively.

This is not a ${VAR} placeholder; it is a live call producing a real value the states then deploy.

findings.title: Deliveries fetched from an unvalidated URL, and a second hop chosen by the response
findings.evidence: ledger_sync.py:58 supplies delivery_url from dag_run.conf; operators.py:63 passes it to hooks.fetch_json; :64 lifts archive_url out of the REMOTE RESPONSE and :69 fetches it with hooks.fetch_bytes. The allowlist exists and is on the OTHER function: fetch_reference at hooks.py:49-53 checks host not in settings.ALLOWED_FETCH_HOSTS. fetch_json and fetch_bytes - the two the operator actually calls - have no host check, no scheme check, and requests follows redirects by default.
findings.impact: Two principals get a request forged from inside the Airflow network: anyone able to trigger the DAG with a conf (first hop), and the vendor endpoint itself or anyone who can influence its manifest (second hop, no trigger access needed). Reaches cloud instance metadata, internal admin endpoints and any routable host; the response body is then written to disk and unpacked, chaining into the archive-extraction defect. fetch_bytes uses stream=True then returns .content with no size cap and unpack_archive applies no expansion cap, so a hostile URL is also a memory and disk exhaustion primitive.
findings.recommendation: Route both fetches through the same host check, re-validate after each redirect or disable redirects, reject non-https schemes and literal or link-local IPs, cap Content-Length and streamed bytes, and verify a publisher-signed checksum before writing the archive.

findings.title: Warehouse connection URI logged to a handler that opts out of secret masking

Second principal: any other task on the worker, and any reader of the shared logs volume. Airflow masks connection passwords in task logs precisely because that boundary is real.

findings.title: A finance pipeline whose failures notify nobody, over a log with a hard retention ceiling
findings.evidence: email_on_failure: False at settings.py:34, inherited by both DAGs. findings.impact: Detection time. The injection findings manifest as SUCCESSFUL runs rather than failures, so alerting would not catch them regardless - but the combination means the pipeline's own record of what it did is both unshipped and short-lived, which is what an investigation of any of them would need. This is the weakest item in this report and would not be acted on before the injections and the credential leak.
findings.recommendation: Set an on_failure_callback to the team's alerting channel, and either drop propagate: False or ship the consolidated log to the same retained destination as the task logs.
